name: Vespid Dynamics Adhesive Restraint Launcher ARL-2 'Flypaper'
description: A launcher that fires capsules of Vespid's industrial-strength cyanoacrylate adhesive compound, which upon impact splatters over a 2-meter radius and bonds to any surface with approximately 800 kg/m² shear strength within 4 seconds of air exposure. Targets struck by the adhesive are effectively glued in place — hands bonded to weapons, feet to floors, bodies to walls. The compound is resistant to solvents and requires a proprietary debonding agent that Vespid sells separately, creating a capture-and-control dynamic where the restraining party controls the only means of release.
legality: Licensed — law enforcement and industrial restraint
specifications:
capsule range: 10-50 meters
splatter radius: 2 meters on impact
bond strength: 800 kg/m² shear within 4 seconds
debonding: Proprietary Vespid solvent only
magazine: 4 capsules
weight: 5.2 kg loaded
capsule weight: 0.8 kg each
adhesive cure time: 4 seconds to full bond
adhesive persistence: Indefinite without debonding agent
story_hooks: A group of people were found adhesive-bonded to the exterior of a corporate building as a protest display — alive, unharmed, but immovable without Vespid debonding agent that the protesters refuse to provide.
Someone has been Flypapering the doors of Tier 3 apartment buildings shut, trapping residents inside — the debonding agent is being withheld until payment is made.

physical_description.visual_profile: A stocky, brutalist launcher resembling a hybrid between a caulking gun and a shoulder-mounted grenade launcher. Its barrel is noticeably wider and blunter than conventional firearms, with a pronounced muzzle brake designed to minimize adhesive blowback. The weapon reads as industrial and purposeful—more tool than gun.
physical_description.dimensions: 56 cm length, 12 cm width at magazine well, 8 cm height at receiver. Barrel length: 18 cm with 4 cm internal diameter.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-heavy when loaded. The 5.2 kg heft is distributed toward the barrel and capsule magazine, making it feel like shouldering a portable industrial apparatus rather than a firearm. Balanced for controlled two-handed deployment.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite body with steel internal pressure channels and aluminum alloy barrel casing to withstand adhesive cure exothermic reactions.
physical_description.finish: Satin-matte industrial gray polymer with brushed steel reinforcement bands around the pressure chamber. Heat-resistant ceramic coating on barrel exterior, showing faint scorch marks from repeated use.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dove gray primary with charcoal accent bands. Safety orange and reflective silver trim around magazine well and muzzle brake for industrial visibility.
physical_description.grip_texture: Deeply textured rubberized polymer grip with aggressive lateral ribs for wet-hand control. Thumb safety lever is knurled stainless steel.
distinctive_features: Large transparent ammo window on magazine showing four 0.8 kg capsules in blue-tinted polymer containment
Vespid's trademark three-pointed wasp emblem embossed on the magazine housing
Pressure release valve with red indicator cap on right side of pressure chamber
Reinforced muzzle brake with asymmetrical porting to direct adhesive dispersal
Integrated heat sink fins along barrel to dissipate cure-reaction thermal signature
Tactical picatinny rail for restraint-assist optics or distance markers
Serial number and production date etched into left side of receiver in precise industrial typeface
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VESPID DYNAMICS corporate logo stamped in metallic silver on the pressure chamber. Model designation 'ARL-2' and 'FLYPAPER' printed below in blocky technical font. Tier 2+ licensing hologram affixed to magazine well.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. Scuffs and adhesive residue around muzzle brake from tactical deployment, but internal mechanisms kept clean. The weapon bears the marks of professional law enforcement or corpo security use—functional and reliable, not showroom.
